success_patterns: Verbatim archive hits (the Barbie clue and the 'Southern pie' clue, which came from TriviaBistro and GitHub dumps) were copied as printed with no extra trimming. Rule 3 already covers this.

A bare one-word proper-noun clue ('Timonium') with only local-business and directory passages was answered with the parent entity the passages repeat on every page (Maryland). The agent did not answer with the clue word or a sub-region such as 'Lutherville-Timonium' or 'Baltimore County'. The skill covers bare date+place and bare name lists but not a bare single place name.

The agents matched the slot type named by the clue noun: 'this island' -> Isle of Man, 'this king' -> Louis XIV with the regnal numeral kept, 'this South American capital' -> Lima, 'this term' -> Apogee. Existing Rule 2 and Rule 4 cover this.

When the clue had a modifier that is not the name of the dish, the agent kept the type noun ('Grasshopper pie'). This follows the head-noun test ('would a key accept the bare word?') over the DELETE-CLUE-WORDS test. The exception exists but has no example showing it wins in this case.

Definition-style clues ('floors that differ by about half a story' -> split-level, 'farthest point from Earth' -> Apogee) were answered with the standard term the passages gloss. The agent did not answer with a descriptive phrase.

patch.reasoning: Most successes were already covered by existing rules. Two gaps appeared. (1) Bare single-place-name clues have no rule, and the agent has to infer the containing state or country. A short conditional bullet near the bare date+place bullet makes this reliable, and it does not collide with other rules. (2) The head-noun exception has no example where an unrelated modifier (an insect name) needs its type noun kept despite the DELETE-CLUE-WORDS test. A one-sentence addition inside the exception settles that conflict without a new bullet. Both edits are short, add no new top-level section, and leave Rule 3 untouched.

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - A bare one- or two-word PLACE name as the whole clue ('Timonium'), with passages that are only local pages, businesses or directories, asks for the larger region that contains it: the U.S. state for a U.S. town or neighborhood, the country for a foreign city. Give the bare name of the level every passage repeats ('Maryland'), not the clue word, a hyphenated census name, or the county.

The same holds when the clue's modifier is an unrelated word that does not name the dish or thing by itself ('Southern pie with an insect name' -> 'Grasshopper pie', since 'Grasshopper' alone names an insect). The head-noun test beats the DELETE-CLUE-WORDS test in these cases.
